title: Rolling prompt-fingerprint regression detector for batching/caching changes
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Summary: Implement a rolling, lightweight detector that flags quality regressions attributable to batching and KV-cache configuration changes by comparing 'prompt fingerprints' and model outputs between baseline and candidate configs. This ticket builds an automated pipeline that combines synthetic benchmark suites with sampled production traces, computes distributional divergence and weighted quality deltas, and wires those signals into an alerting/playback system for on-call and deploy-time gating.

Problem: Changes to batching and KV cache parameters can reduce cost/latency but occasionally degrade output quality in subtle ways (prefix hallucination, increased repetition, truncated completions). Existing evals run offline and are slow to correlate with runtime incidents. We need a fast, continuous detector that: (1) ties regressions to specific config diffs, (2) works with noisy production traffic, and (3) integrates with rollout policies to auto-fallback or block rollouts when appropriate.

Approach: For each candidate config change (canary or global), run a rolling comparison window (default 6 hours) between baseline and candidate traffic/sampled prompts. Create a compact 'prompt fingerprint' (token count, token type ratios, prompt category tag, and embedding centroid) to group prompts. For each fingerprint bucket, pair recent responses from baseline and candidate and compute: JS divergence on token-prob distributions (where available), edit-distance normalized delta, ROUGE/BLEU for well-formed outputs, and a learned automatic quality score (AQS) from our eval model. Aggregate per-bucket deltas weighted by traffic volume and customer priorities to produce a single 'regression score' attributable to the change.

Why unique: Instead of running expensive full-eval suites every time, this uses lightweight fingerprinting and per-bucket aggregates to surface statistically significant shifts quickly and with interpretability (we can show top buckets contributing to the score). The detector supports both pre-deploy evaluation and live canary monitoring.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Detector computes regression score for a candidate config in <10 minutes after a 6-hour window of traffic.
2) False positive rate on historical benign deploys <5% (measured on last 90 deploys).
3) Detector produces a ranked list of top 10 prompt-fingerprint buckets contributing to the score with example baseline/candidate pairs.
4) Integration with rollout controller: if regression score > threshold X (configurable), the rollout is automatically paused and an incident ticket is created.
5) Unit and integration tests covering fingerprinting, divergence metrics, and aggregation logic exist and pass in CI.
success_metrics:
- Time-to-detection median <= 8 minutes after window closes.
- Precision@10 for true regression buckets >= 80% on labeled historical incidents.
- Correlation >= 0.7 between detector score and human eval delta (A/B) on 50 historical regressions.
- Reduction in rollout-induced customer regressions by >= 60% after enabling auto-pause.
test_plan:
1) Offline replay: run detector on last 6 months of release traffic where we know regressions occurred and measure detection latency and precision.
2) Synthetic stress: inject small perturbations (token masking, increased temperature) in candidate config to validate sensitivity across magnitudes.
3) Canary ramp: enable detector for a single internal team and compare alerts to manual evals for two weeks.
4) Blind evaluation: hold back a set of 500 labeled prompts (human scoring) and measure correlation with AQS and detector ranking.
5) Performance tests: ensure detector CPU/memory footprint < 4 vCPU and 8GB for a single-region canary pipeline at 200 RPS sampling rate.
rollout_plan:
Phase 0 (spike): prototype on sampled production traffic, internal-only dashboards.
Phase 1 (canary): run detector on canary rollouts with auto-notify (no auto-pause) for 2 weeks across 3 services.
Phase 2 (guardrail): enable auto-pause for canaries if score > threshold_T1; require reviewer to resume.
Phase 3 (block): for high-severity releases (customer-facing runtime-2.x) enable auto-block + rollback if score > threshold_T2.
Notes: thresholds T1/T2 tuned via historical retrospective analysis. Rollback path uses existing rollout controller (see ENG-50214 for rollback choreography).
monitoring_and_alerts:
- Primary alert: Regression score exceeds active threshold (severity P1). Alert payload includes top 10 fingerprint buckets, sample prompt pairs, and latency delta.
- Secondary alert: sustained JS divergence on a high-volume bucket for 3 consecutive windows.
- Dashboard: 'Config Regression' panel showing score over time, top contributing buckets, and per-customer exposure.
- On-call playbook link: https://confluence.internal.redwood.ai/KB/config-regression-playbook
- Pager escalation: if auto-pause happens, paging to SRE + PM owner within 5 minutes.
- Audit log: every auto-pause/auto-block must create a traceable ticket and include the config diff and detector metadata.
progress_updates: 2025-11-04: Spike implementation completed — built fingerprint hashing and paired-sample extractor. Baseline microbench validated on 1M historical prompts.
2025-11-07: Implemented JS divergence + normalized edit-distance metrics. Early thresholds chosen from ROC analysis; false positives high on short prompts — adding length-aware weighting.
2025-11-12: Ran offline replay on 120 historical deploys: detector caught 14/16 known regressions; opened follow-ups for two missed cases (long-tail prompt categories).
2025-11-14: Added AQS model scoring integration and traffic-weighted aggregation. Working on dashboard panels and rollout controller hook.
Blockers: Access to token probability traces for hosted models is limited for some open-model variants; dependency opened with runtime team to expose compact ngram histograms (ENG-75802).
next_steps: Resolve token-probability access blocker with runtime team (ENG-75802).
Complete integration tests and add CI gating for detector library.
Tune thresholds T1/T2 using 90-day historical replay and finalize rollout_policy YAML.
Schedule canary run with two internal services (expected start 2025-11-20).
